thread:
mira: Heads up — seeing a ~7-9% drop in prefix cache hit rate for hosted models after yesterday's attention-kernel handoff + new 8-bit quant profile rollout. :eyes:
ashwin: ugh. is this across all models or a subset? any region skew?
mira: Primarily affects conversation models (conv-3b/conv-7b) in us-west-2 and eu-west-1. Topline metric is cold warmup hit-rate for first 20 tokens.
lia: do you have the warmup traces? curious if key canonicalization changed with the kernel.
mira: pasted short extract below from perf-ci prefix-hit monitor (avg over 1h windows):
```
model, pre-rollout_hit, post-rollout_hit
conv-3b, 0.72, 0.64
conv-7b, 0.68, 0.60
embedding-only, 0.91, 0.90
```
ashwin: that looks like canonicalization/normalization rather than an eviction rate change. Batching heuristics wouldn't preferentially drop prefix hits that much.
sam: did the kernel swap change pad / seqlen normalization? last time attention tiling changed we saw suffixing issues.
mira: kernel diff attached in PR: compile flags adjusted for fused-attn and we enabled a path that uses 2-stage KV packing for 8-bit runs. suspect key fingerprinting differs when packed.
perf-ci: [bot] rollout: deploy/attn-kernel/v2 -> success (1759989000) regions: us-west-2, eu-west-1, ap-south-1 commit: a1b2c3d
lia: can you grep for differing cache keys? a quick tool: `python -m redwood.tools.kvkeydiff --old-keyfile old.keys --new-keyfile new.keys | head`
mira: ran that, got ~1.3% exact mismatches and ~8% near-miss (trailing nulls / pad ordering). sample below:
```
old: 0x9af3...a2ff
new: 0x9af3...00ff  <-- padding length differs
old: 0x12b4...c0d0
new: 0x12b4...c0d0  <-- same
old: 0x77aa...ff11
new: 0x77aa...ff01  <-- tokenization offset / serializer order
```
ashwin: ok so serializer/pack ordering changed. is this from quantized kernel's packed-kv layout?
mira: yes, the new fused path packs key+value differently to optimize memory. we attempted to canonicalize by trimming pad bytes but missed one codepath (legacy 8-bit fallback).
sam: that explains warmup: clients sending identical prompts hit different cache keys depending on which kernel path served them. needs deterministic canonicalization across variants.
lia: quick mitigation: add a canonicalizer layer in runtime before key hashing that strips trailing 0 padding and normalizes seqlen field. low-risk toggle.
mira: patched a hotfix branch with canonicalizer and ran local sim; hit-rate recovers to baseline in sim (see run).
perf-ci: [bot] perf test results: warmup-hit-rate (simulated) conv-3b: baseline 0.72 -> post-hotfix 0.71 (within noise)
ashwin: can we roll hotfix as canary in us-west-2 only and keep new kernel disabled for canary? or vice versa?
sam: proposal: deploy hotfix + keep kernel v2 enabled, enable canonicalizer toggle for 10% traffic to kernel v2. monitor prefix-hit, latency, token QPS. rollback if hit-rate < baseline - 2%.
mira: agree. I will open a PR for the toggle + monitoring dashboards. cc @perf-ci for alert hooks.
perf-ci: [bot] alert hook configured: warmup-hit-rate-drop -> pager if >3% drop for 5m across 5k requests.
lia: also add a quick check for key-format-version header so we can count which serializer emitted the key. helps long-term.
mira: adding header and a small metric. will push canary in ~30m.
ashwin: thanks. after canary we should add a unit test comparing key generation across all kernel variants and quant profiles so this never regresses.
mira: yup — adding to test matrix.
sam: once canary looks stable, schedule full rollout with a staged ramp and rollback plan.
mira: thanks all — updating thread with links to PR and dashboard when live. :thumbsup:
